Thanks, Mateo. Quick notes from procurement side:

1) PO routing and template
- We use a standard PO template for marketplace sellers. I am attaching the internal PO flow doc to this thread (see PO_Instructions_Nebula.docx that Jenna included).
- Typical fields we require on customer POs: Redwood PO number, marketplace SKU, start/end dates, billing contact, and remit to address.

2) Vendor registration per marketplace
- Usually one vendor account per marketplace provider is required (AWS Vendor Central, GCP Marketplace Seller Console, Azure Commercial Marketplace). Nebula can re-use company legal info, but vendor IDs are separate.

3) Lead time
- Once we have valid W9, signed commercial terms, and vendor banking, we can accept a PO and schedule activation within 5-7 business days for hosted listings. Cross-check: AWS typically needs additional entitlement mapping which can add 2-3 business days.

4) Next step for Jenna
- Please provide a vendor tax ID (EIN), remit address, and bank ACH details via a secure transfer. If you prefer DocuSign we can route an ACH Authorization form.

I will also add a note in HubSpot and create a procurement checklist for this deal.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Head, Partner Procurement

- Bank account name, routing number, account number (we prefer secure upload or DocuSign)

Optional but helpful

Security note: do not email bank details. If you prefer, we will initiate a DocuSign powerform for ACH authorization and vendor banking. Link below.

DocuSign powerform for vendor bank details: https://www.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?PowerFormId=abc-123

Once banking and W9 are validated, we will issue a Redwood vendor ID and provide instructions to map invoices to the marketplace SKU so Finance can auto-reconcile.

Cheers,
